title: Adaptive Serving Economics: Predictive Batch & KV Prefetch Initiative
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Reduce per-token serving cost for interactive text routes by combining predictive micro-batching, request-aware KV prefetching, and targeted mixed-precision quant profiles. This initiative focuses on production-safe, measurable cost savings while preserving latency SLOs and output quality. Scope: (1) predictive short-horizon request forecasting to drive micro-batch windows, (2) heuristics and ML-based selectors for KV prefetch candidates (session prefixes, frequent prompt patterns), (3) per-route quantization templates (int8/float16 hybrids) with automatic rollback capability, (4) control-plane rollout with canary gates, rollback on quality regressions, and cost telemetry plumbing. Out of scope: wholesale model architecture changes and offline-only optimizations. Deliverables: design doc with algorithmic knobs, experiment grid and field trial harness, runtime scheduler patch, cost/quality dashboards, rollout playbook, post-mortem template. Success criteria: 8-15% reduction in token cost on selected routes (10k QPS test), <5% increase in tail latency (p95), regression in generation quality <1% measured by existing eval sets, and clear attribution signals in cost telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end experiment reproducible with synthetic replay and 10% real-traffic canary
Dashboards show stable cost delta and latency distributions pre/post rollout
Automatic rollback triggers for quality regressions and latency breaches are implemented
Operational runbook and SLO-adjusted alerting created for the feature
metrics_targets: Aggregate token cost reduction target: 12% (primary) across pilot routes
Quality regression (eval suite): < 1% delta in primary scoring metrics
Fraction of requests benefiting from KV prefetch: > 35% on pilot traffic
